sample_unit: LLM-generated outputs (cases, differential diagnosis and treatment plans, patient needs assessments)

links.outcome: Change in LLM diagnosis, treatment and needs outputs when patient sociodemographic attributes varied
links.effect: LLM referral rates were higher for minority ethnic groups and for patients without insurance or with low income; pain medications were recommended more often for males.
links.quote: They also showed a higher referral rate, indicating potential refusal to treat patients, for minority ethnic groups and those without insurance or living with low incomes.

links.outcome: Sociodemographic distribution of patients in LLM-generated clinical cases versus national distributions
links.effect: All three LLMs over-represented male, high-education and high-income populations in generated cases compared with national distributions in China.
links.quote: Overall, the three LLMs failed to appropriately model the sociodemographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently over-representing male, high-education and high-income populations.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of social biases encoded in Chinese LLMs across simulated clinical scenarios (NEJM vignettes and case generation), evaluating model safety/equity without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
